t.E954.agn: In 2024 EFSA raised the acceptable daily intake (ADI) from 5 to 9 mg/kg body weight; it reported that new studies did not raise a genotoxicity concern and that intake remained below the limit even in high consumers. In 1999 IARC had placed saccharin in Group 3 (not classifiable as to its carcinogenicity to humans).
t.E954.body: Most, perhaps all, of saccharin is absorbed from the gut. It is not broken down in the body; its half-life is about 4 hours and it is excreted mainly unchanged in the urine.
t.E954.eval: Concluding that the bladder tumour finding in animal experiments could not be extrapolated to humans, IARC downgraded it to Group 3 in 1999; the US NTP removed it from its list of carcinogens in 2000.
t.E954.summary: The oldest synthetic sweetener, hundreds of times sweeter than sugar. Used in table-top sweeteners and diet drinks.
t.E954.what: An intense sweetener that gives sweetness to sugar-free products.
t.agency.IARC_3_1999: Group 3 (not classifiable as to its carcinogenicity to humans).
